title: Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main terms of Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange.
Use or interpret an appropriate PostgreSQL example connected to listen and notify.
Identify one edge case and select a safe way to verify the expected result.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange. Its primary job is to help you connect applications through parameterized drivers and transaction-safe workflows, with migrations tied to releases. The listed PDF subtopics define the coverage expected here; work through them in order and connect each one to an example, edge case and checkable result.
content.why_it_matters: This topic matters because PostgreSQL systems must preserve correct results as data grows and more sessions or services interact with it. Practicing notifications and bulk data exchange teaches you to make assumptions explicit, apply the right SQL or operational tool, and verify behavior instead of relying on a demonstration that only worked once.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep the problem small: connect applications through parameterized drivers and transaction-safe workflows, with migrations tied to releases. A PostgreSQL feature should be chosen for the semantics it provides, not just because it is available. Before executing a change, state the inputs, expected output and boundary conditions. The example below is intentionally small enough to inspect; it illustrates the idea but is not a substitute for a test against your schema and PostgreSQL version.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange
content_blocks.code:
INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price)
VALUES ('SKU-100', 'Notebook', 4.50)
ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE SET price = EXCLUDED.price
RETURNING sku, price;
content_blocks.expected_output: One row for SKU-100 with price 4.50 is returned after the insert/upsert. The table needs a unique constraint on sku.
content_blocks.safety_note: The statement changes data; wrap a lab run in a transaction when appropriate.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Illustrative e-commerce schema: products(sku UNIQUE, name, price). Use a scratch database and inspect RETURNING output.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For a read-only SELECT or inspection command, no reset is needed. For DDL/DML, use a disposable database; capture the starting state, run the example, inspect the result, and ROLLBACK or drop the lab objects as appropriate. Do not use production data or credentials.

task: Create a short practice artifact for “Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange”: explain its goal, show one example linked to “LISTEN and NOTIFY”, state the expected result, and include one edge/failure case and verification method. Use a disposable database or static artifact as appropriate.
hints: Start with the listed subtopics, especially “LISTEN and NOTIFY”, and describe the expected behavior in your own words.
Run or inspect the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior; do not add unrelated features before it is verified.
When the result surprises you, capture the exact SQL/error, check version and permissions, and change one assumption at a time.
expected_output: A reviewable note or query for Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange, with an explanation of “LISTEN and NOTIFY”, expected behavior, and a documented edge-case check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying the example without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Object names, data types, privileges, extensions and data distribution affect database behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: List schema/version assumptions and test with a tiny synthetic dataset first.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a single successful query as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: A happy-path result does not test invalid input, concurrent sessions, permissions, recovery or query performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one negative/edge case and record the evidence that confirms the expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Making a production change directly from a lesson.
common_mistakes.why: DDL, data updates, role changes and operational commands can affect data or availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use an isolated lab, reviewed migration, least privilege, rollback/recovery plan and a second-person review for production.

summary: Notifications and Bulk Data Exchange fits into the broader goal to connect applications through parameterized drivers and transaction-safe workflows, with migrations tied to releases.
Use the curriculum subtopics as a completeness checklist: LISTEN and NOTIFY, Notification payloads and limitations, Bulk import and export.
State the schema/version assumptions and verify one normal case plus an edge case before trusting the result.
